title: Laws of Exponents
student_objective: I can simplify numeric and algebraic expressions using the laws of integral and rational exponents and explain which exponent law I used.
teacher_objective: Diagnose product, quotient, power-of-a-power, zero-exponent, negative-exponent, coefficient-distribution, and rational-exponent misconceptions.

concept_cards.title: Same base multiplied: add exponents
concept_cards.content: For a nonzero base, a^m·a^n=a^(m+n). Keep the base and add the exponents; do not multiply the exponents.

concept_cards.title: Same base divided: subtract exponents
concept_cards.content: For a≠0, a^m/a^n=a^(m−n). Keep the base and subtract denominator exponent from numerator exponent.

concept_cards.title: Power of a power: multiply exponents
concept_cards.content: (a^m)^n=a^(mn). A power raised to another power means multiply the exponents.

concept_cards.title: Zero and negative exponents
concept_cards.content: For a≠0, a^0=1 and a^(−n)=1/a^n. A negative exponent tells you to take the reciprocal; it does not make the value negative.

concept_cards.title: Rational exponents connect powers and roots
concept_cards.content: For real values where the expression is defined, a^(m/n)=(ⁿ√a)^m. The denominator names the root and the numerator names the power.

concept_cards.title: Apply powers to every factor
concept_cards.content: For (ab)^n=a^n b^n and (a/b)^n=a^n/b^n. When a product is inside parentheses, the outside exponent applies to each factor.

product_rule.teacher_signal: Multiplies exponents instead of adding them for same-base products

quotient_rule.teacher_signal: Uses the wrong subtraction order or divides exponents

power_of_power.teacher_signal: Adds exponents instead of multiplying them for a power of a power

power_of_product.teacher_signal: Fails to apply an outside power to every factor

zero_exponent.teacher_signal: Treats a zero exponent as zero instead of one

negative_exponent.teacher_signal: Treats a negative exponent as a negative value instead of a reciprocal

negative_rational_exponent.teacher_signal: Misses either the reciprocal rule or the root meaning of a rational exponent

rational_exponent.teacher_signal: Confuses the numerator and denominator roles in a rational exponent

rational_product_rule.teacher_signal: Does not add rational exponents for same-base products

rational_quotient_rule.teacher_signal: Does not subtract rational exponents for same-base quotients

rational_power_of_power.teacher_signal: Does not multiply rational exponents in a power of a power

multi_variable_quotient.teacher_signal: Does not apply the quotient rule separately to each variable base

multi_step_exponents.teacher_signal: Applies exponent laws in the wrong order in a multi-step expression
